perspective:
Mason’s available information:

- Mason is an accountant at a small community center. Martha is a coworker/personal care aide, and their interactions are mainly professional/work-related.
- While reviewing financial reports, Mason noticed discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high and did not match usual spending patterns.
- Based on this, Mason became suspicious and anxious, believing Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- Mason asked Martha to discuss the report. He told her the numbers did not add up and pointed to the high healthcare expenses.
- Martha said there was likely a reasonable explanation, asked what discrepancies he meant, then looked and said there might have been a misentry. She said she would review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing with Martha, Mason concluded the discrepancies were due to a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved and embarrassed.
- Mason told Martha he appreciated her quick clarification and that it seemed to be a clerical error. Martha said errors happen and she was glad it was cleared up.
- Mason apologized for his initial suspicion, saying he should have asked her first. Martha said it was okay, understood he was being thorough, and suggested double-checking entries next time.
- Mason now believes Martha is competent, but believes recurring clerical errors show the financial management system is inadequate. He feels frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha.
- Mason told Martha the issue was not her management but the current system. He proposed drafting a new, more robust financial system and asked for her input. Martha agreed to help.
- Mason drafted the proposal, hoped it would benefit operations, but was uncertain how management would receive it. He told Martha this.
- Martha encouraged him to present it confidently and said the benefits were clear. Mason planned a detailed presentation and asked Martha to help gather data. She agreed.
- After presenting the proposal to management, Mason felt satisfied but exhausted and believed he had done everything he could. He told Martha the presentation went well and that it was now up to management.
- Martha praised his work and suggested he take time off. Mason thanked her and planned to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping for good news.
- Martha wished him a good break and offered to help while he was away.
- Mason does not yet know management’s final decision.
